official.deadline_note: The separate Stanford graduate degree program application is due by the earlier of the degree program's deadline for KHS applicants or 1 December 2026. Stanford MBA applicants must apply in Round 1 only, the sole round aligned with the KHS admission timeline. Programs whose deadlines fall after 1 December 2026 still require submission by 1 December 2026 to stay KHS-eligible.
official.application_cycle: 2027 cohort (application closed 6 October 2026); the 2028 cohort application opens summer 2027
official.status_note: The official site states: 'The KHS application to join the 2027 cohort is now closed. The KHS application to join the 2028 cohort will open in summer 2027.'
official.tuition_coverage_note: A fellowship applied directly to cover tuition and associated fees, during each of the first three years of graduate study. For degree programs longer than three years (MD, PhD, DMA, MSTP MD/PhD, JD/MBA), funding is based on the graduate degree program's standard funding commitment, which varies by department and school.
benefits: A fellowship applied directly to cover tuition and associated fees
A stipend for living and academic expenses (such as room and board, books, academic supplies, instructional materials, local transportation, and reasonable personal expenses)
A travel stipend intended to cover an economy-class ticket for one annual trip to and from Stanford
A one-time relocation stipend for newly enrolling scholars, intended to offset some of the costs associated with relocation to the area and/or technology purchases
Scholars in their second and third years may apply for supplemental funds to support academic enrichment activities (e.g., conference travel)
Up to three years of King Global Leadership Program programming complementing the degree
eligibility: No restrictions based on age, college or university, field of study, or career aspiration; citizens and residents of all countries are encouraged to apply, with no quotas by discipline, program, or world region.

You must apply to, be accepted by, and enroll in a full-time Stanford graduate degree program (including but not limited to DMA, JD, MA, MBA, MD, MFA, MPP, MS, or PhD), starting it in the same year as Knight-Hennessy Scholars.
You must have earned, in January 2020 or later, a U.S. bachelor's degree or its equivalent from a college or university of recognized standing.
For applicants who served in the military, the eligibility window is extended by two years: a degree earned in January 2018 or later to enroll in 2027.
Current college students are eligible if the first degree will be earned by September 2027; within the window, no preference is given based on recency of the degree.
Endorsements from colleges, universities, or other institutions are not required.
requirements: Submit the Knight-Hennessy Scholars online application by 6 October 2026, 1:00 pm Pacific Time - the same deadline for all applicants regardless of the degree program.
Submit a completely separate Stanford graduate degree program application by the earlier of the degree program application deadline for KHS applicants or 1 December 2026.
There is no application fee for Knight-Hennessy Scholars, but you must pay any application fee required by your degree program; KHS cannot provide fee waivers for degree program applications.
Recommendation letters are due by the application deadline, but you must still complete and submit your own application on time even if letters have not yet arrived.
If your degree program requires test scores (including English proficiency), submit them to KHS by the later of your degree program's application deadline or the KHS application deadline.
Finalists must attend Immersion Weekend, March 5-6, 2027, barring unforeseen circumstances and/or immediate family obligations.
documents: Online application form (contact information, biographic and demographic details, employment, activities and awards, and other context)

Transcripts of undergraduate (and graduate, if applicable) performance for each institution attended for one academic year or longer; unofficial transcripts are accepted, and study-abroad credits need not be uploaded if included on the transcript
Diploma or other document evidencing the degree conferred and conferral date, if the transcript does not show them
Official English translation for any transcript or degree document in another language
Standardized test scores required by the graduate degree program(s), including English proficiency results where required
Two recommendation letters submitted online by the recommenders

Three short answers and one essay: intentions (250 words), engaging with a different perspective / acting with courage / falling short of expectations (250 words combined), eight improbable facts (150 words combined), and 'Connect the dots. How have the influences in your life shaped you?' (550 words)
Video statement (by invitation, January), online individual interview (mid-February 2027), and Immersion Weekend attendance (March 5-6, 2027) for finalists
selection_criteria: Independence of thought - visionary thinkers who are curious, open-minded, analytical, eager for cross-cultural perspective, and excited to boldly and creatively address the world's important challenges
Purposeful leadership - courageous leaders who are ethical, decisive, resilient, driven to achieve meaningful results, and motivated to inspire others to effect positive change at scale
Civic mindset - collaborative community members who are humble, empathetic, trustworthy, oriented to act in service of others, and deeply passionate about contributing to the greater good
There is neither a typical nor a prototypical Knight-Hennessy scholar; each cohort is diverse by design and no two candidates are equally strong across all criteria
coverage: Tuition and associated fees for up to three years, depending on degree length
Living and academic expenses: room and board, books, academic supplies, instructional materials, local transportation, and reasonable personal expenses
One economy-class ticket for one annual round trip to and from Stanford
Partial relocation costs to the Bay Area and/or technology purchases, via a one-time relocation stipend
Supplemental academic enrichment funding such as conference travel, by application in years two and three
application_method: Create the Knight-Hennessy Scholars application and the Stanford graduate degree program application(s) concurrently, as early as possible; the two are separate applications reviewed by separate committees.
Register both recommenders in the online application as early as possible so the system can send each a personalized submission link.
Complete and submit each application by its own deadline, then use the KHS Application Status page for permitted post-submission updates.
Submit all KHS materials in English through the online application; materials sent by email or postal mail are not accepted.
official.application_route: Two separate but concurrent online applications - one to Knight-Hennessy Scholars and one to each Stanford graduate degree program - each submitted independently by its own deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: No restrictions based on citizenship or residency; citizens and residents of all countries are encouraged to apply, with no quotas by world region. Applicants with DACA status, no formal citizenship in any country, or otherwise undocumented are eligible to apply for graduate study and matriculate at Stanford University and Knight-Hennessy Scholars.
official.international_eligibility: Eligible. KHS imposes no nationality or citizenship restriction; international applicants must hold the equivalent of a U.S. bachelor's degree from a college or university of recognized standing and must meet the requirements of the specific Stanford graduate program, which are set by the Office of Graduate Admissions rather than by KHS.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Must enroll in a full-time graduate degree program at one of Stanford's seven schools. Degree programs NOT eligible for KHS: the Honors Cooperative Program, Master of Liberal Arts, Doctor of Science of Law (JSD), Master of Legal Studies (MLS), coterminal degrees, and current Stanford PhD students adding an MA or MS degree in their PhD discipline.
official.duration: Up to three years of funding, depending on degree length: MA, MBA, MFA, MPP, MS, JSM, MLS, LLM up to six academic quarters (1-2 years); JD nine academic quarters (1-3 years); MD up to 11 quarters, excluding the summer quarter of year 1 (1-3 years); PhD and DMA up to 12 quarters - nine academic quarters and three summers (1-3 years).
official.description: Knight-Hennessy Scholars is a fully-endowed, multidisciplinary leadership development program for graduate students at Stanford University, described by Stanford as the largest university-wide, fully endowed graduate fellowship in the world. Scholars from around the globe receive up to three years of financial support to pursue graduate studies at any of Stanford's seven schools.
official.program_type: Graduate fellowship / multidisciplinary leadership development program
official.english_requirement: KHS sets no minimum English proficiency score of its own, but if the Stanford graduate degree program to which you are applying requires English proficiency results, you must submit them to KHS as well. All Stanford graduate degree programs accept TOEFL; most but not all accept IELTS; the MBA Program is the only program that also accepts PTE. For most Stanford graduate degree programs the minimum TOEFL score for admission consideration is 90 (taken before 21 January 2026) or 5.5 (taken on or after 21 January 2026), and the minimum IELTS score for admission consideration is 7. Some departments accept only scores obtained within the last 18 months, others 24 months.

No dollar amount is published by KHS, so the funding amount fields are null by rule.

applicant_utility.summary: This fellowship pays your Stanford tuition outright and adds a living stipend, an annual round-trip ticket and a one-time relocation payment, so it removes almost every cost barrier to a Stanford graduate degree - worth the effort even though only about 87 scholars are named per cohort. Treat it as two applications that must both land: the KHS form argues leadership and civic character, while the separate department application argues academic fit, and KHS explicitly will not read your department file for you. Build your calendar backwards from 6 October (KHS) and 1 December (department), because missing either one forfeits the fellowship even if the other file is perfect. Note that the window is short and closed: the 2028 round does not open until summer 2027, so transcripts, essay drafts and recommender relationships prepared in advance are the difference between a rushed file and a strong one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent graduates - first bachelor's degree earned January 2020 or later - with a documented record of leading change beyond coursework, ready to commit to a full-time Stanford graduate degree starting the same year.
application_readiness_checklist: Write both deadlines into your own timezone: KHS closes at 1:00 pm Pacific on 6 October, and the department's own KHS-applicant deadline (or the 1 December outer limit) governs the separate Stanford application.
Confirm your intended program's deadline and application fee directly with the department - Stanford deadlines vary by program and KHS issues no fee waivers for them.
If you are targeting the MBA, plan for Round 1 only; later rounds are not compatible with KHS eligibility.
Register two recommenders early in the portal, choosing people who supervised, taught or worked alongside you recently rather than the most senior names you know.
Check that your transcript prints the degree conferred and the conferral date, and pull a diploma copy if it does not.

Order official translations early for any non-English transcript or recommendation letter; unofficial transcripts are accepted, but translations must be official and uploaded as a single document with the original.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the Stanford degree application after 1 December (or after the program's own KHS deadline) - the degree admission may still succeed but KHS eligibility is permanently lost.
An essay that is fluent but impersonal: the committee is scoring independence of thought and authentic voice, and answers that read as polished or AI-smoothed actively work against you.
Recommenders who are senior but never observed your work closely - KHS states plainly that character references without supporting evidence do not improve a candidacy.
Being strong on paper but never verified as competitive by the degree program: KHS advances only applicants the department confirms are still in contention.
Finalists who cannot attend Immersion Weekend on 5-6 March 2027 - apart from genuine emergencies, non-attendance ends the selection.
Overlooking the degree-recency gate: a first bachelor's degree earned in 2019 or earlier (2017 or earlier with military service) disqualifies you no matter what later degrees you hold.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Taxes on the fellowship stipend, which KHS does not reimburse; your Stanford degree program's application fee; standardized test registration fees; any part of a longer degree beyond the three funded years (MD years 4-5, PhD year 4 onward) that your department's own funding commitment does not cover; and relocation, visa and settlement costs beyond the one-time relocation stipend.
document_audit: Transcripts may be unofficial but must cover every institution attended for a year or more and must show the degree conferred plus the conferral date.

Recommendation letters must arrive in English and must not be written, drafted, edited, translated or submitted by you - you affirm this in the application, and a paid service or friend may translate but you may not.
A non-English transcript or recommendation needs the original and its official translation combined into a single uploaded document.
The KHS application locks on submission: afterwards you can only update test scores, recommenders, your resume and your intended degree program, so proofread everything before you press submit.
alerts: The 2027 cohort application closed on 6 October 2026 at 1:00 pm Pacific - the official site now reads 'The KHS application to join the 2028 cohort will open in summer 2027', so any listing showing this round as open or closing soon is stale.
KHS offers no deferrals at all; if you cannot enroll in the admission year you must reapply from scratch.
You cannot be admitted to KHS without a separate offer from a Stanford graduate degree program - KHS has no power to admit you to Stanford.
Applying to KHS does not reduce your chances of Stanford admission, so the KHS application is close to a free option alongside your department application.

Degree program deadlines are the hidden killer: programmes with deadlines after 1 December still require a 1 December submission, and current Stanford PhD students may only apply in their first year for second-year entry.
Some Stanford graduate programmes are excluded outright from KHS eligibility - check the Honors Cooperative Program, MLA, JSD, MLS and coterminal rules before planning around this fellowship.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit your own KHS portion by the 6 October deadline even with recommenders outstanding, then push outstanding scores and letters through the Application Status page; department decisions can arrive anywhere from December to April, video statement invitations go out on a rolling basis through January, finalists are named 27 January, interviews run mid-February and Immersion Weekend is 5-6 March 2027.
